newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad-based EMU drop - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad-based EMU drop - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union, including Italy, Spain and Sweden, continued their decline over the past five trading days despite a modest recovery last week, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
In the past five trading days, market prices indicated that the perceived probabilities of Spain, Sweden, Italy and the UK joining Germany in EMU in 1999 all fell.

The perceived probability of Italy taking part dropped 8.0 percentage points this week to 56 percent, the first time it has been below 60 percent since late November. Spain fell 7.0 points to 59 percent and Sweden declined 5.0 points to 60 percent.
Over the past month, EMU expectations are down most in Spain and are 19.0 points below peaks four weeks ago. Italy is down 10.0 points over the month and Sweden is1 down 7.0 points.
Elsewhere, the perceived probability of the UK joining Germany in EMU in 1999 fell 3.0 points over the week but remains low overall with an estimated 35 percent chance.
Denmark rose 3.0 points to 48 percent.
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week, the calculator showed.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
